title: Pachinko Bayes
summary: Drop sixty balls through gates and count: total probability of a red landing, then Bayes’ theorem for two and three gates.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Conditional probability as a ratio of counts
learningOutcome: The student can find P(E) by total probability over two or three causes, and use Bayes’ theorem to find the chance a landing came from a given cause, as a ratio of counts.

levels.title: How many red?
levels.adds: Baseline: P(E) = ΣP(Aᵢ)P(E|Aᵢ), found by counting the red balls through each gate and adding (Section 13.5.2; Ex 13.3 Q1; Example 15).
hints: Count how many balls go through each gate.
Take the red fraction of each gate’s balls.
Add the red counts over the gates.

levels.title: Which gate?
levels.adds: New: P(Aⱼ|E) = P(Aⱼ)P(E|Aⱼ) / ΣP(Aᵢ)P(E|Aᵢ): the red balls from one gate over all the red balls (Ex 13.3 Q2 to Q5; Examples 16, 18).
hints: Count the red balls that came through the gate asked about.
The chance is the first count out of the second.

levels.title: Three gates
levels.adds: New: Bayes’ theorem with three causes, where the total red count has three terms (Ex 13.3 Q6, Q7, Q11; Examples 17, 19, 20).
hints: Count the red balls through all three gates.
Add them for the total red landings.
Put the asked gate’s red count over that total.

misconceptions: P(gate | red) is the same as P(red | gate)
A fraction can be set only in lowest terms
Every gate is equally likely to be the source
